theory.intro: The number plane has two axes that cross at the origin $(0,0)$, dividing it into four quadrants. Each point is given by an ordered pair $(x, y)$.
facts: The first number is the **$x$-coordinate** (across); the second is the **$y$-coordinate** (up or down).
Right of the origin is **positive $x$**, left is **negative $x$**; up is **positive $y$**, down is **negative $y$**.
The point $(0,0)$ is the **origin**, where the axes meet.
steps: Move up/down by the $y$-coordinate, then mark the point.

foundation.solution_text:
Read $3$ units left, so $x=-3$.
Read $4$ units up, so $y=4$.
$A=(-3,4)$

A point on the $y$-axis has $x=0$.
The vertical coordinate is $-3$.
$C=(0,-3)$

foundation.question_text: Point $D$ is $2$ units left and $5$ units down from the origin. Write its coordinates.

foundation.solution_text:
Move $2$ units left and $3$ units up from the origin.
The labelled point is $P$.

development.solution_text:
The point is $5$ units right and $4$ units down.
$G=(5,-4)$

development.question_text:
Write the coordinates of point $J$ on the $x$-axis.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.65]
\draw[gray!30,very thin](-5,-4)grid(5,4);\draw[<->](-5.5,0)--(5.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[<->](0,-4.5)--(0,4.5)node[above]{$y$};\foreach \n in {-5,...,-1,1,...,5}{\node[below,font=\scriptsize]at(\n,0){$\n$};}\fill(-4,0)circle(2.5pt)node[above]{$J$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
development.solution_text:
The horizontal coordinate is $-4$.
A point on the $x$-axis has $y=0$.
$J=(-4,0)$

development.question_text: A drone is $6$ units right and $2$ units down from the origin. Record its position as an ordered pair.

Which two points share the same $x$-coordinate? Give both coordinates.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.65]
\draw[gray!30,very thin](-5,-5)grid(5,5);\draw[<->](-5.5,0)--(5.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[<->](0,-5.5)--(0,5.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(-3,4)circle(2.5pt)node[above left]{$K$};\fill(-3,-2)circle(2.5pt)node[below left]{$L$};\fill(4,-3)circle(2.5pt)node[below right]{$M$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
development.solution_text:
$K$ and $L$ lie on the same vertical grid line.
$K=(-3,4)$ and $L=(-3,-2)$

development.question_text: A point $T$ shares its vertical grid line with $U(-4,1)$ and its horizontal grid line with $V(2,-5)$. Write the coordinates of $T$.
development.solution_text:
$T$ has the same $x$-coordinate as $U$: $x=-4$.
$T$ has the same $y$-coordinate as $V$: $y=-5$.
$T=(-4,-5)$

mastery.question_text: Lina plots $N(-3,5)$ by moving $3$ units right and $5$ units down. Identify both errors and state the correct movements.
mastery.solution_text:
A negative $x$-coordinate means move $3$ units left.
A positive $y$-coordinate means move $5$ units up.

mastery.question_text: Points $P(-2,4)$, $Q(3,4)$ and $R(3,-1)$ are three corners of a rectangle whose sides follow the grid lines. Find the fourth corner $S$.
A point has a negative $x$-coordinate, a positive $y$-coordinate and is equally far from both axes. Give one possible coordinate pair and explain why it works.
mastery.solution_text:
One possible point is $(-4,4)$.
It is left of the $y$-axis, above the $x$-axis and $4$ units from each axis.
